content.value:
A Subsystem represents one hardware mechanism: the drivetrain, an arm, or a claw.

It owns the motors and sensors for that mechanism.

Other code accesses the hardware only through the subsystem's public methods. It is good practice to never expose the hardware to the outside of the subsystem.

Every subsystem in SolversLib extends SubsystemBase.

Open DriveSubsystem.java.

It extends SubsystemBase and has an empty constructor, empty drive() and stop() methods, and an empty periodic().

Right now it's a skeleton — you'll fill it in.

Declare two private DcMotor fields: leftMotor and rightMotor.

Only this subsystem should touch its own motors, so keep them private.
In the constructor, get the drive motors from the HardwareMap.

Fill in drive() with three parameters: forward, strafe, and turn.

Use the same drive code as you did before.

steps.title: Add stop() and leave periodic() empty

content.value:
Fill in stop() — set both motors to 0.

Leave periodic() empty for now. It's called every tick by the scheduler and is where you'd read sensors or update PID.

In SubsystemOpMode.java, create a DriveSubsystem in initialize() — the constructor auto-registers it with the scheduler.
